evidence: The microstructural evolution depending on the Ru intermixing ratio in Ru–AlN thin films was characterized using an X-ray diffractometer (XRD) and a bright-field scanning transmission electron microscope (BF-STEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) element mapping. The film thickness was analyzed by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and the film composition was analyzed by 9.0 MeV He2+ Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) and Auger electron spectroscopy (AES). The sheet resistance was measured using a four-point probe. The microstructures of the films were studied using an XRD with Cu-Ka radiation at 1.5405 A˚ and a BF-STEM. Further, TEM-EDX element mapping was performed to investigate the relationship between microstructural evolution and electrical resistivity of films.
